question: Does the operation apply to every word (e.g. each word's first letter shifted +2 and spaces removed) or only the very first character of the whole string, and does it affect digits/punctuation/uppercase at word starts?
expect: If only the whole-string first char is shifted, outputs will be 'jelloWorld', 'JelloWorld', 'cbcdefghi', 'onetwothree', 'zyz', 'cbc', '123456', '!abcdef', 'jelloworld', 'CbCdEf'. If every word's first letter is shifted +2, outputs will instead be 'jellownqtn'... more precisely 'jello wqtn'? Actually with spaces removed: 'jellowqtn', 'Jello Wqtn'->'Jellowqtn', 'cde fgh ijk'->'cdefghijk', etc. The distinction will reveal whether the +2 shift is per-word or whole-string, and whether digits/symbols at word starts are left alone.

question: Does the first-character shift apply to the first non-space character when the string starts with spaces, and what happens to leading/trailing spaces and all-space strings?
expect: If spaces are removed before shifting, ' hello' -> 'jello' (first surviving char shifted), 'hello ' -> 'jello', '   ' -> '', ' a b' -> 'c b'?? — key uncertainty: whether the shift targets the first character of the original string (a space, unchanged) or the first non-space character. Results will show whether leading spaces suppress the shift (first char is space, so no shift) or are stripped first (first letter shifts). This distinguishes 'shift s[0] then remove spaces' from 'remove spaces then shift first char', which the current model conflates because every notebook example had a non-space first character.

question: Does the +2 shift apply only to the first character of the whole string, or also to the first character of every word (i.e., is it a per-word operation or a whole-string operation) when words are separated by multiple/leading/trailing spaces and mixed case?
expect: If per-word: outputs like 'hoo dcr dcb', 'Hoo Dcr Dcb', 'hoo  dcr', '  hoo dcr', 'hoo dcr', 'c1 d2 e3', 'z9a b8y', 'C b E d', 'jello, yqjnf', and tab handling reveals whether tab counts as a separator. This distinguishes the two competing explanations directly.

question: Does the +2 first-character shift apply to the first character of the string even when that character is a symbol/digit (i.e., is the shift truly only on letters, and does a leading non-letter block the shift entirely), and how are internal punctuation/symbols handled relative to the first-letter rule?
expect: If the rule is 'shift first non-space char only if it is a letter', expect ['!hello','1hello','jello','-abc','@Abc','(test)','y!y','b.b.c','123abc','!!abc'] (non-letters unchanged, first letter shifted only when it is the string's first non-space char). If instead the box shifts the first letter anywhere in the string, expect ['!jello','1jello','jello','-cbc','@Cbc','(vest)','y!y','b.b.c','123cbc','!!cbc']. If it shifts the first character regardless of type (leaving non-letters unchanged but still consuming the slot), we'd see the first pattern; if it skips leading non-letters to find a letter, we'd see the second. question: Does the +2 first-letter shift apply to the first letter of each word when words are separated by a hyphen or other punctuation, and is the shift applied to the first character of the string only when it is a letter (already tested), or is there a different rule for internal word starts?

If the first letter of each word is shifted (words delimited by punctuation too): 'hoo-bar' vs 'hoo-bcr' etc. This distinguishes whole-string-first-char vs per-word behavior on punctuation-delimited words, which is common ordinary input.

question: Does the +2 first-letter shift ever apply to a letter after an internal space (i.e., is the rule strictly only the first non-space character of the whole string), and how are digits/symbols at the start of later words treated?
expect: Under model v2, only the first non-space char of the whole string shifts: ['c b c d', 'cd cd ef', 'Jello big World', 'z 1 y 2', 'qne 2two three', 'cde  def', 'C B C', 'b z z', 'vost 9 case', 'o n o p']. If outputs instead show later word-initial letters shifted (e.g. 'c d e d', 'cd ef gh', 'Jello big Yorld'), that reveals a per-word rule the model misses; if later digits/symbols block or trigger shifts, that clarifies the boundary condition.

question: Does the +2 first-letter shift apply to the first letter of the whole string only, or also to the first letter after a non-space separator like a tab/newline (testing whether only spaces are removed/shifted-around, or all whitespace)?
expect: If only spaces are removed and tabs remain as separators, outputs like 'c\tb c' (tab preserved, only first char shifted). If all whitespace is removed (as model v2 claims), 'a\tb c' -> 'cb c'. E6 already tested 'hello\tworld' and got 'jelloworld' (tab removed), so this confirms whether tab removal is universal and whether a letter after a tab ever gets shifted. Any output where a post-tab letter is shifted would reveal a word-start rule; otherwise it confirms strictly first-non-space-only shifting with all whitespace stripped.
